thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary window 23: sustained p95 latency increase on runtime-group=prod-us-east (from ~120ms -> ~640ms) detected at 2024-08-05T02:00:01Z. Affected model-route: llama-13b-varying-kernels. Error rate stable, but throughput dropped ~40%. Auto-fallback to kernel-compat variant seen on ~12% of requests.

sarah (oncall): ack. I'm taking this. tagging @michael for kernel selector/rollout context and @lee for handoff if we need a rollback.

michael (eng-sre): looking. initial checks: no infra CPU/GPU OOMs, kv-cache evictions spiked around same time. suspicion: recent routing change in release wave-7 that nudged a subset to the new kernel selection logic + adaptive batching tweak.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0812-042 (severity: P2). Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/runtime-latency. Pager duty: sarah (oncall).

priya (support): we've got two customers (AcmePay, GoodFood) reporting slow responses in prod. AcmePay SLA ticket #8342 on hold, they called in. BJ from AcmePay asking if this is being rolled back.

sarah (oncall): can we try the release kill-switch (safe rollback path) to cut the new routing? If it stabilizes, we can do a controlled rollback. michael, can you propose the minimal flip?

michael (eng-sre): propose: flip feature flag `routing.kernel_selector.v2` -> false for prod-us-east. This will force older kernel selection path and avoid the new batching heuristic. Command (runbook snippet):
```bash
# toggle feature flag via ffctl
ffctl set routing.kernel_selector.v2 false --env=prod --region=us-east --reason="inc-1719500001 latency spike"
# sanity: curl -s https://flagproxy.prod/internal/v1/flags/routing.kernel_selector.v2 | jq .value
```

michael (eng-sre): I'll run the flip in 2m unless objections. I'll also pre-warm a small canary against kernel-compat before flipping all traffic.

sarah (oncall): go for it. priya: please update AcmePay that we're actively mitigating and that a rollback is planned if the flip doesn't help.

michael (eng-sre): pre-warming canary now against older kernel-compat variant: `curl -X POST https://canary-run.prod/infer -d '{"input":"ping"}'` returns within 140ms.

michael (eng-sre): flipping flag now.
```bash
ffctl set routing.kernel_selector.v2 false --env=prod --region=us-east --note="inc-1719500001"
# response: ok
```

incident-bot: Feature flag change detected: routing.kernel_selector.v2=false by michael at 2024-08-05T02:04:10Z.

michael (eng-sre): watching metrics (p95, throughput, kv-eviction-rate).

(2 minutes later)

michael (eng-sre): p95 dropping toward baseline: 170ms -> 130ms over 90s. throughput climbing back. kv-evictions down. kernel fallback rate reduced from 12% -> 1.2%.

sarah (oncall): nice, keep observing for 10m. priya, call AcmePay back with ETA ~10m and say we've applied a mitigation.

priya (support): on it. calling now. will update ticket #8342.

(10 minutes later)

sarah (oncall): after 10m steady state, metrics look good across prod-us-east. I recommend we do not perform a full rollback; we should keep the FF off and stage a controlled release after kernel selector fixes.

michael (eng-sre): agree. root cause appears to be an interaction between new batching heuristic and a specific kernel path that increases KV thrash by favoring longer prefix batches; patch in progress (small selector guard). Will open PR with tests.

lee (oncall-next): I'll pick this up for overnight monitoring and runbook follow-through. sarah, handing off: I've read the thread and can take post-mortem ownership.

sarah (oncall): thanks @lee. handoff complete. summary for notes: mitigation applied (FF off), customer notifications sent, no data loss, SLA alerts acknowledged.

acct-notify-bot: Notifying billing/enterprise team that AcmePay had elevated latency during window 02:00-02:12 UTC. Ticket #8342 updated.

michael (eng-sre): next steps: PR for selector guard, add regression test in canary harness to simulate high prefix reuse, and add a quick metric alert: kernel_fallback_rate > 5% for 5m.

priya (support): AcmePay confirmed their flows are OK now, they lowered the priority but want a follow-up in the postmortem.

sarah (oncall): closing immediate incident work. leaving notes in INC-2024-0812-042 and assigning postmortem to michael + lee. will set targeted postmortem meeting.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2024-0812-042 marked RESOLVED by sarah at 2024-08-05T02:18:00Z.

michael (eng-sre): adding one more note: need to consider KV cache metrics per-route in the console to spot this earlier. filing REDW-ops ticket.

lee (oncall-next): will watch overnight, will escalate if any regressions. :thumbsup: 

sarah (oncall): thanks team.
